subject: Third-party visibility & data flow confirmation
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.inference>
To: Julia Hart <julia.hart@finhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Third-party visibility & data flow confirmation

Hi Julia — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

What we heard from you:
- FinHealth needs SOC 2 Type II evidence and a high-level subprocessor map for vendor risk intake.
- GDPR & HIPAA considerations apply for portions of the workload; residency for certain datasets should be EU-only.
- Procurement will run the standard vendor security questionnaire and requires a mutual action plan (MAP) to keep timeline tight.

What we’ll provide by EOD Thursday (09/16):
1) Export-ready subprocessor matrix (service, purpose, data accessed, region, contractual flow) — attachment: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v2.xlsx
2) High-level data flow diagram showing where PHI/PII might transit — attachment: dataflow-diagram-v3.svg
3) SOC 2 Type II summary and redacted report where allowed — attachment: SOC2-TypeII-redacted-2025.pdf

Questions / asks for you: 
- Can you confirm whether the HIPAA scope is all FinHealth customers or a subset of workloads? That will determine the BA/contracting approach.
- Please point me to the procurement contact and any internal intake ticketing (Ben if you have a vendor id or HubSpot deal).

Proposed MAP milestones:
- 09/16: Redwood delivers subprocessor matrix, diagram, SOC2 summary.
- 09/17–09/21: FinHealth runs questionnaire and flags follow-ups.
- 09/24: Joint sync to review any high-risk subprocessors and BA terms.

I’ve CC’d Marissa (legal) and Karthik (security) so they can jump on specifics. If this looks right, I’ll upload the MAP to HubSpot and share a DocuSign link for the confidentiality addendum.

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.inference | +1 (415) 555-0173

Attachments: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), dataflow-diagram-v3.svg (diagram stub), SOC2-TypeII-redacted-2025.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Julia Hart <julia.hart@finhealth.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurement@finhealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:22:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Third-party visibility & data flow confirmation

Alex — thanks for the follow-up and the clear plan. A few quick things from our side: 

1) HIPAA scope: it applies to a subset — specifically the claims ingestion and clinical notes features. We’ll enumerate fields that are PHI in the questionnaire.
2) Procurement loop: procurement@finhealth.com is the right inbox; they’ll expect a MAP and the redacted SOC 2.
3) Residency: for the clinical workloads we require EU data residency (processing in eu-west regions). Other control plane metadata can remain in US region.

I’m attaching what we can share now (redacted SOC 2 and a short vendor intake checklist). Our security team will start the questionnaire review tomorrow.

One ask: can Redwood confirm whether you encrypt customer data at rest with customer-managed keys (CMKs) or service-managed keys? Also please call out whether any analytics/telemetry pipelines receive PII.

Thanks,
Julia Hart
Head of Security Programs | FinHealth
julia.hart@finhealth.com

---- Forwarded Attachment(s): SOC2-TypeII-redacted-2025.pdf (pdf stub), FinHealth-Vendor-Intake-Checklist.pdf (pdf stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.inference>, Julia Hart <julia.hart@finhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Third-party visibility & data flow confirmation

Julia / Alex — quick technical note to help with the questionnaire: 

- Cloud footprint: Redwood uses AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2) for hosted inference and persistent stores; we also run GCP (europe-west1) for customers who require EU residency. For Dedicated customers we can deploy into a customer VPC (bring-your-own account) or Redwood-managed VPC in customer's region.
- Encryption: data at rest is encrypted by default using AWS KMS. For customers requesting CMKs we offer a KMS integration option (customer-managed keys) for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted accounts we support a customer-managed KMS binding via our managed key partnership (depends on contract).
- Telemetry/analytics: aggregated telemetry is pseudonymized and does not contain raw customer payloads. There is an optional opt-in telemetry stream for model performance that can be disabled per customer.

I’ve attached a simple data flow diagram showing where PHI could be present depending on the integration pattern (direct ingest -> inference runtime -> optional long-term embeddings store). Happy to walk through the diagram on a follow-up call.

—Karthik
Principal Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.inference

Attachment: dataflow-diagram-v3.svg (diagram stub)
